title: Eero showing solid red LED
shortDescription: The Eero is not connected to the internet and shows a solid red status light.
fullDescription:
A solid red LED on an Eero device indicates the gateway unit has lost its WAN connection and cannot reach the internet. This affects the entire mesh network, and all downstream nodes will also go offline.

Common causes include a modem issue, an unplugged Ethernet cable, or an ISP outage. The Eero app will show the network as offline until connectivity is restored.

causes.cause: Loose or damaged Ethernet cable between modem and Eero

symptoms: Solid red LED on gateway Eero

fixSteps.title: Check ISP status
fixSteps.instruction: Use cellular data to visit your ISP's outage page or call support to confirm the service is up.

fixSteps.title: Power-cycle modem and Eero
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the modem for 60 seconds, plug it back in, wait until it's fully online, then power-cycle the Eero gateway.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Ethernet cable
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat the Ethernet cable between modem and Eero. Swap with a known-good cable if the red light persists.

whenToCallPro: Call your ISP if the modem will not come online after a reboot.

faq.q: Does a red LED mean the Eero is broken?
faq.a: No. It almost always indicates a WAN/internet problem upstream, not a hardware failure.

title: Eero node reported offline in app
shortDescription: A secondary Eero node is unreachable from the gateway and shown offline.
fullDescription:
When the Eero app flags a node as offline, that unit is either unpowered, too far from the nearest mesh neighbor, or experiencing a firmware hang. The rest of the mesh will continue serving clients, but coverage in that node's area will drop.

The node's LED is typically off or blinking white when this happens.

causes.cause: Node unplugged or on a dead outlet
Node too far from nearest mesh peer

fixSteps.title: Verify power
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the Eero is plugged in and the outlet is live. Try another outlet.

fixSteps.title: Reboot the node
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the Eero for 30 seconds, then plug it back in. Wait up to 2 minutes for it to rejoin the mesh.

fixSteps.title: Relocate closer
fixSteps.instruction: If the node still fails to join, move it closer to the gateway or another online Eero to re-pair, then relocate.

whenToCallPro: If the node never rejoins after a factory reset, contact Eero support for replacement.

faq.q: How long should I wait for a node to come back online?
faq.a: Give it 2-3 minutes after power-up. If it doesn't rejoin, reboot or relocate it.

title: Eero firmware update hanging
shortDescription: The firmware update does not complete and the network stays degraded.
fullDescription:
Eero automatically installs firmware overnight. Occasionally the update process stalls because a node is offline, has poor backhaul, or loses power mid-update.

When stuck, the app may show 'Update pending' for days or nodes may reboot repeatedly.

fixSteps.title: Force update from app
fixSteps.instruction: Open Eero app > Settings > Software version > Check for update and tap Update.

fixSteps.title: Reboot the entire network
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle all Eeros at once, starting with the gateway. Wait 5 minutes before retrying update.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: If update still won't complete after 24 hours, open a chat with Eero support from the app.

whenToCallPro: Contact Eero support via the app if a manual update retry fails repeatedly.

faq.q: Can I skip an Eero firmware update?
faq.a: No, Eero firmware updates are mandatory and installed automatically.

title: Secondary Eero lost mesh backhaul
shortDescription: A node can no longer reach the gateway over wireless or wired backhaul.
fullDescription:
Eero mesh nodes maintain a backhaul connection to the gateway either via Ethernet or wirelessly. If this link breaks due to distance, interference, or a bad cable, the node drops from the mesh.

Clients previously served by that node will roam to another Eero if one is in range.

causes.cause: Node out of wireless range of any peer
Bad Ethernet cable on wired backhaul

fixSteps.title: Check placement
fixSteps.instruction: Aim for no more than 40 feet between nodes, with at most one wall in between.

fixSteps.title: Reboot the affected node
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle to force it to reselect the best backhaul.

fixSteps.title: Swap backhaul cable
fixSteps.instruction: For wired backhaul, test with a known-good Cat 5e or Cat 6 cable.

whenToCallPro: Hire an installer if you need to run Ethernet through walls for a wired backhaul.

faq.q: How do I check mesh link quality?
faq.a: In the Eero app, tap the node and look at 'Connection to Eero' – it should say 'Good' or 'Excellent'.

title: Eero online but no internet for clients
shortDescription: Clients connect to Wi-Fi but cannot reach the internet.
fullDescription: The Eero LED is white and the mesh is healthy, but DNS or DHCP issues prevent clients from actually reaching sites. This often happens after ISP changes or when double-NAT is introduced by a modem-router combo.
symptoms: Connected Wi-Fi but no pages load
Works on some devices, not others

fixSteps.title: Bridge ISP modem
fixSteps.instruction: Put the ISP gateway into bridge mode so the Eero handles NAT. Contact ISP if bridge option isn't exposed.

fixSteps.title: Change DNS
fixSteps.instruction: In Eero app > Network Settings > DNS, switch to Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) or Google (8.8.8.8).

fixSteps.title: Restart everything
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle modem, then Eero. Allow each device to fully boot before powering the next.

whenToCallPro: Call your ISP for help putting the modem in bridge mode.
videoSearchQuery: Eero no internet double NAT fix

faq.a: It's when two routers both perform NAT, causing port and connectivity issues. Bridging the ISP modem eliminates it.

title: Eero app cannot find or pair device
shortDescription: During setup, the Eero app fails to detect the new unit.
fullDescription: When adding a new Eero, the app uses Bluetooth to discover the device. Pairing fails if Bluetooth is off, the phone is too far, or the Eero's LED isn't flashing blue.

causes.cause: Eero LED not in pairing state (flashing blue)

symptoms: App says 'We couldn't find your Eero'
LED is white or off instead of flashing blue

fixSteps.title: Enable Bluetooth and Location
fixSteps.instruction: Turn on Bluetooth and grant Location permission to the Eero app.

fixSteps.title: Reset the Eero
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the reset pinhole for 15 seconds until the LED flashes yellow, release, and wait for blue flashing.

fixSteps.title: Move phone closer
fixSteps.instruction: Stay within 3 feet of the Eero during discovery.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed – contact Eero support if reset doesn't restore pairing.

faq.q: Why does the Eero app need Location permission?
faq.a: Android requires Location permission to use Bluetooth Low Energy scanning, which Eero setup relies on.

title: Websites fail to resolve on Eero network
shortDescription: Names don't resolve but raw IP pings may still work.
fullDescription: DNS issues on Eero are usually caused by an unreachable upstream resolver or a misconfigured custom DNS. Eero Secure/DNS over HTTPS may also interfere if the upstream is blocked.
symptoms: Ping by IP works, by name does not

fixSteps.title: Revert to automatic DNS
fixSteps.instruction: Eero app > Network Settings > DNS > Automatic.

fixSteps.title: Pause Eero Secure
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disable Eero Secure content filtering to rule it out.

fixSteps.title: Try public DNS
fixSteps.instruction: Set manual DNS to 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 and retest.

whenToCallPro: Call ISP if automatic DNS also fails – may indicate WAN-level problem.

faq.a: Eero Secure subscribers can enable encrypted DNS resolution upstream.

title: Eero throughput capped below subscribed speed
shortDescription: Measured speeds are much lower than ISP plan.
fullDescription: The Eero Internet Speed Test returns values well below your plan. Causes include using a non-gigabit Eero for a gigabit plan, a slow modem, or a client on 2.4 GHz only.

causes.cause: Eero model maxes below ISP plan (e.g., Eero 6 ~500 Mbps)
Modem downlink not provisioned for full speed
Test client on 2.4 GHz or old Wi-Fi

fixSteps.title: Confirm Eero model limits
fixSteps.instruction: Eero 6 WAN tops near 500 Mbps; use Eero Pro 6/6E or Eero Max 7 for multi-gig plans.

fixSteps.title: Test wired
fixSteps.instruction: Plug a laptop directly into the gateway Eero LAN port and run speedtest.

fixSteps.title: Check client radio
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure test client supports 5 GHz or 6 GHz and is close to the Eero.

whenToCallPro: Contact ISP if wired speed to modem is below plan.

faq.q: Why does Eero 6 cap near 500 Mbps?
faq.a: Its WAN port and CPU cannot sustain gigabit throughput – upgrade to Pro 6/6E or Max 7 for higher plans.

title: Eero warm to touch and rebooting
shortDescription: Device becomes hot and cycles itself to protect hardware.
fullDescription: Eeros are fanless and rely on passive cooling. Placement in enclosed cabinets, direct sunlight, or stacking other electronics can push internal temperatures past safe limits, triggering unplanned reboots.

causes.cause: Faulty power adapter feeding wrong voltage

fixSteps.title: Relocate
fixSteps.instruction: Place Eero on an open surface with airflow on all sides.

fixSteps.title: Avoid stacking
fixSteps.instruction: Don't place anything on top of or immediately under the Eero.

fixSteps.title: Replace adapter if suspect
fixSteps.instruction: Use only the official Eero adapter; replace if damaged.

whenToCallPro: Contact support if overheating persists in a ventilated location.

faq.a: Mildly warm is normal; hot to touch plus reboots indicates thermal issue.

title: Eero not entering factory reset state
shortDescription: Holding the reset button does not return the Eero to setup mode.
fullDescription: A proper factory reset requires holding the reset button until the LED flashes red/yellow, then releasing. Short presses perform only a soft reboot. If the LED never enters pairing mode, the device may be tied to a previous account.

causes.cause: Reset button not held long enough
Device still linked to previous owner account

symptoms: LED returns to white after release
App can't detect Eero for setup

fixSteps.title: Hard reset procedure
fixSteps.instruction: Hold reset for 15+ seconds until LED flashes red, then flashes blue. Release.

fixSteps.title: Remove from previous account
fixSteps.instruction: If purchased used, ask previous owner to remove device from their Eero app.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: Eero support can unlock an orphaned device with proof of purchase.

whenToCallPro: Contact Eero support for account-locked devices.

faq.a: 15+ seconds for a full factory reset until LED flashes red.
